about: The `sendidexpr` of a <cancel> is a string computed from the machine's fields when the cancel runs, and names the id of the delayed send it removes: `which` holds `a` to begin with, so `cancel` removes the send `a` and `b` comes due, and `pick.b` makes the same <cancel> remove the other. An id no send holds cancels nothing and raises nothing: `pick.none` empties `which`. An operation that fails cannot be evaluated, so `overflow` raises error.execution and removes neither send. Both sends wait 200 ms and every check stands at least 50 ms from a deadline. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: both sends are armed, and neither is due
the wait is over: only `b` comes due
armed again, and `which` is made empty
an empty id names no send: nothing is removed and nothing is raised
the id cannot be computed: error.execution is raised and no send is removed
the name is `b`, and the sends are armed again
the same <cancel> now removes the send `b`
